gaps.sentence: You ___ better take some cash — the stall does not take cards.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' warns about a sensible action: had better take.

gaps.sentence: You ___ told me — I would have kept the evening free!
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' plus the participle criticizes something that did not happen: should have told.

gaps.sentence: He ___ be hungry — he has just eaten a three-course meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' rules out the possibility based on evidence: can't be hungry.

gaps.sentence: You ___ pay for children under six — entry is free for them.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' expresses absence of necessity: needn't pay.

gaps.sentence: He ___ have driven so fast on that icy road — he is lucky to be unhurt.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' criticizes dangerous past behavior: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to hand in essays by Friday at the latest.
gaps.hint: ought to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' takes the full infinitive, so only 'ought' fits before 'to': ought.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have taken the wrong turning — the signpost was knocked down in the storm.
gaps.explanation: 'May have + participle' offers one possible explanation of a past event.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather not comment until the investigation is over.
gaps.hint: a polite refusal with would rather not
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather not' declines politely: would rather not.
